name: MJB ADHD
headline: Understand it. Treat it. Get the next decision made.
tagline: A guidebook that connects ADHD science, treatment, care routes and lived experience — where every claim shows what kind of evidence stands behind it, and every route ends in something you can use.

howto.d: Six entrances, each starting from something a real reader is trying to do.
Every page opens at a one-minute summary. The depth dial reveals six layers, from quick understanding to the evidence itself.
Coloured labels say whether a sentence is guidance, research, an institution's position, a patient observation, a hypothesis or a known gap. Tap a label to see its sources.
Hover a link to preview it. The map beside each page shows what leads in and where to go next, and your path is kept for this session.

shortcut.title: Treatment helped, and now you can't get it?
shortcut.text: Go straight to the continuity route: what to ask, who owns the next decision, and a request you can copy.

entrances.title: Understand your experience
entrances.question: I recognise this, but why?
entrances.blurb: Start from the difficulty you notice — memory, time, starting tasks, pain, movement — and work towards useful observations.

entrances.title: Understand treatment
entrances.question: What do these medicines actually do?
entrances.blurb: How ADHD medicines act, what the evidence says about benefit and harm, and what happens when treatment stops or restarts.

entrances.title: Navigate care
entrances.question: Who decides what happens next?
entrances.blurb: Find the owner of the next decision, ask for it in writing, and separate clinical requests from complaints, records and safeguarding.

entrances.title: Explore evidence
entrances.question: Is ADHD biologically real — and how?
entrances.blurb: Genes, brain development, the dopamine and noradrenaline machinery, treatment trials, and the open questions still being argued.

entrances.title: Lives and accountability
entrances.question: What happened, and what is still unanswered?
entrances.blurb: Responsibilities, official findings, safeguards, a non-personal case register and Matthew’s separate personal record.

entrances.title: Method and tools
entrances.question: How do I read this guide?
entrances.blurb: Evidence labels, the source register, and tools you can fill in and take to an appointment.

labelDefs.guidance: What a national guideline, regulator or product licence says. Guidance shapes practice; it does not guarantee a particular prescription.
labelDefs.research: A finding from published research. Check the study design: a trial, a registry comparison and a case report carry very different weight.
labelDefs.institution: What an NHS body or service has said or decided, in its own records. It shows their position, not that the position is correct.
labelDefs.patient: What a patient observed or reported. Recorded by a clinician or not, it remains a report until measured or independently corroborated.
labelDefs.hypothesis: A proposed explanation that has not been tested. Included because it generates useful questions — never as a basis for changing treatment alone.
labelDefs.contested: Two or more accounts of the same event disagree. Both are shown; neither is treated as settled until records resolve it.
labelDefs.missing: A source that should exist and has not been obtained or checked. Absence from reviewed records does not mean the event did not happen.
labelDefs.finding: A formal finding by a body with authority to make it — a coroner, ombudsman, regulator or court.
